fact: Club of Mozambique (AIM) reports that the government's new telecommunications regulations were strongly criticised by unnamed civil society bodies and opposition parties as allowing internet shutdowns on national security grounds, and that named journalist and press freedom activist Tomas Vieira Mario publicly condemned the minister's defence on Facebook and called for the regulations to be overhauled; as_of is the document's published date, the minister having spoken the day before.

OONI measurements show ISPs in Mozambique blocked Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp from 29 October to 14 November 2024 amid post-election protests, after the communications institute (INCM) announced internet restrictions.

Human Rights Watch reports mobile and internet access was restricted from 25 October 2024 after post-election protests, with social media blocked, and operators confirmed restoration on 18 November 2024.
